name: St Andrews
tagline: The home of golf and one of Scotland's oldest universities, a small, windswept coastal town with an outsized place in history.

intro: St Andrews is genuinely known worldwide as the home of golf, its Old Course a place of pilgrimage for players long before most visitors ever set foot in the small Fife town surrounding it.

That single reputation genuinely undersells the place — St Andrews is also home to Scotland's oldest university, founded in 1413, and the substantial ruins of what was once the largest cathedral in Scotland, a reminder of the town's earlier role as the country's religious capital.

Most visitors genuinely spend a day or two here, walking the Old Course's famous Swilcan Bridge, the cathedral ruins and the windswept West Sands beach, all within a genuinely compact, walkable town centre.

whyVisit.intro: St Andrews' case rests on genuinely being the literal birthplace of golf, layered with deep medieval and academic history.

attractionsIntro: St Andrews' essential sights combine the literal home of golf with substantial medieval and academic history.

attractions.name: The Old Course

image.alt: The Old Course at St Andrews

attractions.text: Genuinely the oldest golf course in the world, played since the 15th century and still a working public course today.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a public right of way crosses parts of the course — you can walk sections even without playing.

attractions.name: Swilcan Bridge

image.alt: The Swilcan Bridge on the Old Course at St Andrews

attractions.text: Genuinely golf's most iconic crossing, a small stone bridge photographed by generations of the sport's greatest players on their final round.
attractions.tip: Genuinely early morning offers the best chance of an uncrowded photo.

attractions.name: St Andrews Cathedral ruins

image.alt: The ruins of St Andrews Cathedral

attractions.text: Genuinely once the largest cathedral in Scotland, its substantial ruins still convey real scale from the town's medieval religious importance.
attractions.tip: Genuinely climb St Rule's Tower, included with entry, for sweeping views over the town and coast.

attractions.name: St Andrews Castle

image.file: File:The ruins of St Andrews Castle.jpg
image.alt: The ruins of St Andrews Castle overlooking the coast

attractions.text: Genuinely a dramatic clifftop ruin with a real, gruesome history, including a rare survivable siege tunnel and bottle dungeon.
attractions.tip: The genuinely siege tunnel and mine are a highlight, included with the standard entry ticket.

attractions.name: The University of St Andrews

image.alt: The historic buildings of the University of St Andrews

attractions.text: Genuinely Scotland's oldest university, founded in 1413, its historic buildings woven throughout the town centre itself.
attractions.tip: Genuinely free walking tours of the historic campus run regularly in season.

attractions.name: West Sands Beach

image.file: File:The West Sands, St Andrews - geograph.org.uk - 7987631.jpg
image.alt: West Sands Beach at St Andrews

attractions.text: Genuinely a wide, windswept beach made famous by its opening scene in Chariots of Fire, backing directly onto the Old Course.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a bracing but rewarding walk any time of year, not just in summer.

attractions.name: The R&A Clubhouse

image.file: File:R&A Clubhouse, Old Course, Swilcan Burn bridge.jpg
image.alt: The R&A Clubhouse overlooking the Old Course

attractions.text: Genuinely golf's spiritual headquarters, the historic clubhouse overlooking the Old Course's first tee and Swilcan Bridge.
attractions.tip: Genuinely one of the most-photographed buildings in golf, even without stepping inside.

thingsToDo.title: Walk West Sands Beach

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely bracing, scenic walk along the wide beach made famous by Chariots of Fire's opening scene.

thingsToDo.title: Wander the historic university streets

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely pleasant way to spend an hour, exploring Scotland's oldest university woven through the town's medieval streets.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely join a free student-led walking tour for real insider context.

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely hands-on historic experience, crawling through a rare surviving siege mine and tunnel beneath the castle.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a St Andrews visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Check genuinely Old Course playing hours if hoping to walk the public right of way.
Visit genuinely early morning for the best photos at the Swilcan Bridge, before crowds build.
Buy genuinely a combined ticket for the cathedral and castle to save on entry costs.
Wear genuinely comfortable shoes for the town's cobbled medieval streets.
Pack a proper windproof layer for West Sands, which genuinely lives up to its bracing reputation.
Book accommodation genuinely ahead during major golf tournament periods.

faq.q: How many days do you need in St Andrews?
faq.a: One day genuinely covers the Old Course, cathedral and castle comfortably; an overnight allows a more relaxed pace.

faq.q: Can you play golf on the Old Course?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely, though tee times are highly sought after and often require booking many months ahead or entering a ballot.

faq.q: Do you need to golf to enjoy St Andrews?
faq.a: No, genuinely not — the cathedral ruins, castle, university and beach are all worthwhile regardless of interest in golf.

faq.q: What is St Andrews known for?
faq.a: Genuinely as the home of golf, alongside Scotland's oldest university and substantial medieval cathedral ruins.
Yes, genuinely very — the entire town centre sits within a comfortable walk, with no car needed for sightseeing.

faq.q: Can you visit St Andrews as a day trip from Edinburgh?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it's about an hour and a half's drive, making it a workable, if full, day trip.
